questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Edinburgh, because it is a good university and a beautifull city. It was also nice, that they speak english and that i got an Erasmus scholarship.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty straightforward.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They do a comprehensive welcome week, when you arrive with events happening every hour of every day. They take you on walks around the city, introduces you to the universities societies, and there are pizza dinners with you student advisors and academic cohorts. I hav free pizza every day that week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I found it through the university. It took two minutes to sign up on their website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think it is possible to live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I live in a dorm, and I can highly recommend. It is a good way to meet a lot of people, and it is nice to have your friends close by for sponataneous hangouts. I only lived with postgraduate and other exchange students. It is my understanding, that people renting a room in private accomodation felt a bit isolated, and I know a few who moved from private accomodation to our dorm, because they saw how much fun we were having. 

The only downside is, that it is very expensive. I think it is worth it though.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You look at the course list. Then you wish 10 courses or so. A month before the exchange they give you some of you courses. If they clash, you have time to change your courses upon arrival in edinburgh. It is very easy to make course changes. You just text your student advisor. You can switch courses until third week of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My student advisor was very helpful and always replied fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successfull. I got the courses, I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much. You can figure it out, when you get there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty similar to back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In the physics courses, they prefer to tech using slides rather than blackboards. I prefer slides. In general, they focus a lot on physical intuition and experimental results and often skips the long - if not all - mathematical derivations. 

Also, all the exams are two hours and without notes. You are only allowed to bring a calculator, so if you have one already, it is a good idea to bring it to Edinburgh.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics
Nuclear and Particle Physics
Numerical Recipies
Introduction to Computer Systems (Informatics course)
Geometry (Math course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Condensed Matter Physics: Well structured and interesting course. Lecturer is nice. Can recommend.

Nuclear and Particle Physics: This course is horrible! Each part is only about 12 lectures, which means that everything is very rushed through and on the surface. There is not time to motivate or explain any of the results, which just have to be accepted. Both lecturers are bad at explaining and have no sense of connecting the course prerequisites to the content. The notes are useless. 

Numerical Recipies: Well structured course. You learn some nice numerical tools, but not anything groundbreaking compared to the mandatory computing courses in Copenhagen. Is a lot of work throughout the semester. It is worth focussing on the checkpoints rather than the workshops.

Geometry: Very good and inspirering lecturer! Involves som cool math and explains some tools with great application in physics. Can highly recommend!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have pretty much every society, you can imagine available to all students. Everyone are very nice, and they are easy to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I joined the Canoe Club and MathSoc FC.

I can highly recommend both!! It is a great way to meet some local students.

The Canoe Club does kayak trips on "white" rivers around Scotland. You don't need any experience, and it is great fun. It is basically river rafting, which is insane, but very thrilling and an amazing experience. An exciting way to engage with the nature and see some of Scotland. Everyone are very nice, and they do a lot of socials. 

MatchSoc FC is the football team asociatioated with the Math Society. The have five-a-side practices and a game on the weekend every week. it is a great way to play some footy and play with some true, british football boys. Everyone are very nice and they do socials.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed going on hikes in the beautifull landscape. There a lot of nice spots close to Edinburgh. I went to the Pentland Hills and Pitlochry. 

Otherwise I played football and went on kayak trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the societies. THey are all run by local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I attended a few Ceilidhs. It is a traditional scottish repetitive partner dance. They play some folk music and someone tells you the steps. It is a bit like Lancier, only more fun. A must do!

I also enjoyed going to the pub to watch football games and attend pub guizzes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't know. DO IT

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most important: dont worry! Especially about accomodation and courses. They don't allocate university accomodation before two/three weeks before the semester starts, and everyone I know got something. I also know people, who went there without having a place to live, and the unviersity helped them get something instantly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was the friends I made. Edinburgh is a very international city, so I met people from all over the world, and I had so much fun getting to know them and their culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I chose some pretty difficult courses, so at times I found it chanllenging to balance academics with enjoying my time abroad. It is maybe worth picking an easy course or two.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
